title: 1996 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement: How many subsets containing three different numbers can be selected from the set \(\{89, 95, 99, 132, 166, 173\}\) so that the sum of the three numbers is even?

solutions.text:
The set has \(4\) odd numbers—\(89,\) \(95,\) \(99,\) and \(173\)—and \(2\) even numbers—\(132\) and \(166.\) A sum of three is even only with two odds and one even, since three evens is impossible with just two available.

The count is \(\binom{4}{2} \cdot \binom{2}{1} = 6 \cdot 2 = 12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: With only two even numbers available, an even sum must use two odd numbers and one even
There are \(4\) odd and \(2\) even numbers; choose \(2\) of the \(4\) odds and \(1\) of the \(2\) evens
